author: Mark Atwood
text:
Decision-record bead in tension with bd:JMAP-sf5h.25 (memory-DoS bound on Deserialize). Defer to human for paired resolution.

.9 says: defend the #[serde(try_from = String)] decision; keep the adapter, do NOT add a custom Deserialize impl.
.25 says: switch to a custom Visitor impl so visit_str can length-check BEFORE allocation, closing the memory-DoS posture at the protocol boundary.

The two cannot both stand as-recommended.

CONCRETE: under the status quo, serde_json::from_reader(payload_of_a_billion_bytes) allocates a 1 GiB String before from_hex rejects it for length. Under from_str (where the input is already a &str owned by the caller), the deserializer can hand visit_borrowed_str the existing slice — but the type's TryFrom<String> still takes an owned String, forcing serde_json to allocate even though the borrow path was available. A custom Visitor with visit_str (and visit_borrowed_str delegating to it) can length-check the &str before any allocation in the type's own code, and would short-circuit the from_reader DoS path provided serde_json itself bounds its internal buffer — which it does NOT by default; that's a caller-side responsibility (e.g. .max_size on the http body reader).

RECOMMENDATION: close .9 as 'reconsidered in light of .25'; resolve .25 with option (c) (custom Visitor + brief allocation-bounds docs note). The change is local to the Sha256 type, no public-surface impact (the serde derive's #[serde(try_from, into)] attribute is replaced with a hand-rolled impl Serialize + impl Deserialize). Subsumes bd:JMAP-sf5h.22 (which already landed with the move-not-clone fix in TryFrom<String> — the custom Deserialize would route through validate(&str) directly without ever calling TryFrom<String>; .22's fix stays correct for other call sites).

CASCADE IF (a) APPLIED [keep status quo, accept DoS posture]: close .9 as 'declined-keep-adapter'; close .25 with option (b) docs-only resolution (add # Allocation bounds rustdoc).

CASCADE IF (c) APPLIED [custom Visitor + docs]: close .9 as 'declined-supersede'; close .25 with the new impl + docs.

Both are public-API-stable; the choice is engineering taste (one-place validation in TryFrom<String> vs. visitor-path length pre-check). I lean toward (c) because the DoS posture concern in .25 is a concrete protocol-boundary issue, not just an idiom; serde validation centralization (.9's argument) is preserved by having the Visitor itself call the shared validate(&str) helper that bd:JMAP-sf5h.22 already extracted.
